questions.question: Give three reasons why cities grow in particular places, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Cities grow next to rivers, like Cairo on the Nile; at ports on the coast, like Lagos on the Atlantic; where minerals are found, like Johannesburg where gold was discovered; or where the government is, like Nairobi, Kenya's capital.

questions.question: Describe Cairo and Lagos: where each is and why it is important.
questions.expected_answer: Cairo is the capital of Egypt, in the north-east of Africa, on the River Nile near its delta; it is one of Africa's biggest cities and the pyramids of Giza are nearby. Lagos is Nigeria's biggest city, in West Africa on the Atlantic coast; it grew as a port and is Nigeria's centre for business, music and film.

questions.question: Explain how Johannesburg and Nairobi began.
questions.expected_answer: Johannesburg grew very quickly after gold was discovered on the Witwatersrand in 1886, and people came to work in the mines. Nairobi began in 1899 as a stop on the railway from Mombasa on the coast to Lake Victoria.
